Ch3_P1.NarrativeText: The board wanted the critters thinned out. Small ones, quick ones, the kind that throw stones and run away.
Ch3_P1.Title: Someone Needs It

1.Line: Whoa, this critter dropped a whole sack of food... what a lucky day!

3.Line: It leads to a cave by the river, I think I should go and find it.

2.Line: Oh, wait, what is this? A map? Is this a treasure map?

8.Description: Take what the altar gives back

2.Description: Follow the map to the cave by the river

1.speaker: Klepon
1.text: Ha... that voice. You are not one of ours. I am old, I am blind, and I have not set foot beyond this cave in years. What harm could I possibly do to you?

3.speaker: Klepon
3.text: Well, whatever it is that has brought you all the way down here, sit, sit. I have had nothing to listen to but the river for a very long time...

2.speaker: Klepon
2.text: You smell of bread, and water... the little one brings me food from time to time, so that sack upon your back must be his. Did he hand it to you? He has never entrusted it to a stranger before.

2.ChoiceLabel: A goblin?! Don't move, I warn you!

1.ChoiceLabel: I found this sack, and a map to here.

3.ChoiceLabel: What things? Like this altar stone?

4.ChoiceLabel: Why do you want it whole again?

2.DialogueGreeting: Who is there? You are dripping all over my floor... far too heavy for the little one, I should think. Come in, come, sit where it is dry!

1.Line: The little one who brought him bread... that was one of them, wasn't it? One of the thirty I cut down for a job off the board...

2.Line: He is sitting in the dark waiting for him, and he is not coming back... the least I can do is bring his stone back to him.

7.Description: Set the four pieces into the altar

1.Line: Four slots and four pieces, and every single one of them fits like it never left.

3.Line: Whoa, the stone on the altar lit up!

2.Line: Human, Elf, Beastmen, and theirs, side by side... the old king's stone, whole again.

1.Line: That is all four of them... I should get back to the cave.

Ch1_P5.NarrativeText: You wake up in the tavern. Feels like the road home is longer than you remember it. Smoke still hangs over the valley. Where the house stood, there's only wreckage and the fields are torn open. The door, the hearth, everything gone. And your mother along with it.
Ch1_P5.Title: The Empty House

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

3.Description: Talk to the stranger at your plot
3.DialogueGreeting: Ah, there you are. When the smoke rose past the ridge I came as fast as these old legs would allow.

1.speaker: Theron
1.text: Breathe first, child. I will tell you what little I know.

3.speaker: Theron
3.text: I was away in the hills when it began. By the time I saw the smoke, it was already over.

2.speaker: Theron
2.text: A portal opened at Dewdrop, and a beast came out of it. Lycaros. The whole village fought it.

5.speaker: Theron
5.text: Gone is not dead. Remember that, child.

4.speaker: Theron
4.text: Your farm was not spared, and your mother... we searched, child, every corner, and there is nothing. She is simply gone.

7.speaker: Theron
7.text: Now, up you get. The best thing for you today is work, there's plenty of it.

6.speaker: Theron
6.text: Did she leave anything behind, a note, a book, anything at all? If anything turns up, bring it to me first.

9.speaker: Theron
9.text: I'll watch over you, child... That's what an elder is for.

8.speaker: Theron
8.text: Clear the wreckage and keep whatever you find, it's still your home, and it's still yours to raise.

Ch1_P2.NarrativeText: Marta is strict and practical, she won't say she loves you, she'll hand you a hoe instead... She teaches you everything fast, like there's a deadline only she can see.
Ch1_P2.Title: Marta's Lessons

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

4.Description: Get a Watering Can (from Leaf, or Rendall at night)

3.Description: Get a Hoe (from Leaf, or Rendall at night)

1.speaker: Marta
1.text: You can swing a weapon. Congratulations! Now learn something that actually keeps you alive, farming!

4.speaker: Marta
4.text: She opens at dawn and shuts her shop at midnight. If you're late, Rendall keeps the basics behind his bar for a little more. Here's just enough Tria, so come back with tools, not snacks!

3.speaker: Marta
3.text: There's an Elf in Dewdrop Village named Leaf, she runs a farming shop.

2.speaker: Marta
2.text: Farming starts with tools. A hoe and a watering can. I'm not made of those, so go buy them.

2.DialogueGreeting: Good, you're here. Now sit, actually... don't. You won't be sitting for a while.

Ch2_P4.NarrativeText: A sharper blade, a new skill, a fed chicken. You almost feel safe. Rendall has watched you go door to door, and he has something to say about it.
Ch2_P4.Title: Mind Who's Listening

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

4.Description: Take a job from the village quest board

1.speaker: Theron
1.text: The goblins have been restless since the portal. More at the fence every week. Rendall's board is full of work, and half of it goes untaken.

3.speaker: Theron
3.text: Start at the village board. Look for small jobs and honest coin for now, the Junkyard can wait.

2.speaker: Theron
2.text: You are young, and you are trained now, that is sufficient.

5.speaker: Theron
5.text: And, child... if you find anything strange out there, writing or markings, anything not goblin made, bring it to me first.

4.speaker: Theron
4.text: Go to the Junkyard once your strength is back.

3.DialogueGreeting: There you are, steadier every day. Sit down, child.

1.speaker: Rendall
1.text: They're not wrong, work got me through worse years...

4.speaker: Rendall
4.text: Now eat. It's on the house, and the bread is fresh out of the oven.

3.speaker: Rendall
3.text: Soldiers drink here most nights and they tend to talk about all kinds of things, so if I hear anything, I'll tell you.

2.speaker: Rendall
2.text: You've been asking around about your mother. Good, keep asking. Just mind who is listening when you do...

2.ChoiceLabel: Everyone keeps telling me to work.
2.DialogueGreeting: There you are. Sit down, you look like you've carried the whole weight of the village today.

Ch3_P3.NarrativeText: The second stone lit up. Two more are in the town past the gate, but Klepon will want to hear about this one first.
Ch3_P3.Title: Nobody Answered

1.Description: Tell Klepon what the stone on the cliff gave back

1.speaker: Klepon
1.text: Remarkable... the little one said the man completed two in a single week, and after that, he went on to the town. So that is where you shall go next.

3.speaker: Klepon
3.text: But it went cold when the old king died, and cold it remained... except for one occasion. Years later, on one such occasion, the little one came running one morning, shouting that the sky above the town had been coloured once more during the night!

2.speaker: Klepon
2.text: Back when I could still see, that town never slept. Every roof breathed cyan and magenta coloured steam, day and night, until the whole sky above the town was painted with it. From the Crown Mound, it looked as though the town were ablaze with colour.

1.ChoiceLabel: It did, that's two done now.
Colored for whom? And why did it turn cold?

3.ChoiceLabel: Then I will paint it again.

2.ChoiceLabel: And that one night? What happened?

1.DialogueGreeting: Ha! I can hear two of them knocking about in your bag. So the stone upon the cliff lit for you as well?

1.Line: A whole town built to paint the sky?

2.Line: He stood on that tower and turned the sky cyan and magenta, I want to see what that man saw...

3.Description: Look at the socket on top of the water tower

1.Line: An empty socket on top of the tower.

3.Line: That wheel has some structure in the middle, like the pedestal in the heaps. That one might have the rune stone.

2.Line: One slot on it, big enough for something to be stacked up, there is a stone wheel on the other tower.

2.Description: Find the water tower in Geartown

7.Description: Set the three cubic stones on the empty socket (0/3)

1.Line: Water, wind, fire, all three are in.

3.Line: When I turn one stone, the one next to it turns too, so I cannot just swap them around... I will have to work it out.

2.Line: And to make steam you need fire at the bottom, wind to feed the fire, and water on top of it all.

1.Line: That is all three of them, let's get back up to the tower.

9.Description: Take the rune from the wheel pedestal

8.Description: Turn the stones until the town produces steam

1.Line: Steam! Every chimney in the town is breathing it, cyan and magenta, one after another!

3.Line: I hope somebody up there sees it this time...

2.Line: The wheel on the other tower is turning on its own now, and the rune stone in the middle is glowing. That must be the reward.

Ch4_P3.Title: The Little House

1.Description: Open the door of the little house

1.Line: Hnngh... thud, thud... THUD!

4.Line: There's a little round window next to the door, but it's way too small for me to climb through.

2.Line: It won't budge... something is holding it shut from the inside, so is somebody still in there?

3.Description: Find out which frog can reach the latch

1.Line: The latch was pushed shut from the inside, but nobody is in here, and that window is way too small for a grown person, so how did they ever get out?

2.Description: Tell Grandpa Dutzie about the door

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Oh no, do not look at me like that, I am a fat old frog and I would get stuck in that window until winter.

2.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
2.text: But my grandchildren could fit through it, and I think those three have been following us since the river, so let me call them.

2.ChoiceLabel: It's locked, but there's a window.
2.DialogueGreeting: Krokk... I saw that, you pushed so hard your whole face went red, and that door did not even creak.

5.Description: Look at the paper on the floor

1.Line: A page of calculations with no clear writing... only three spots of color, so were they trying to mix three colors of this spell potion together?

4.Description: Look at the bottles by the cauldron

1.Line: Hmm... some of these bottles got knocked over, like they were in a hurry, and there are so many colorful bottles here... is this a spell potion?

7.Description: Brew the spell potion in the cauldron

1.Line: Wait... is this a journal about opening a portal? Let me check...

4.Line: They must have opened a portal with this spell potion to get out of here... I'll try mixing it the way I think they did.

3.Line: A journal about opening a portal with a spell potion, bottles of it knocked over everywhere, a page of calculations with three spots of it... and a door locked from the inside with nobody in this house.

2.Line: This person was mad, I can't understand any of it, but I'm sure they spent a very long time researching how to make a portal with a spell potion.

Ch4_P3.NarrativeText: This is the little house where Grandpa Dutzie saw her last, and the dagger that nearly hit her is still stuck in the door.

Ch1_P4.NarrativeText: Marta's last test. 'There's a scrapheap out past the village, and there you'll find living machines, weakened by rust. Bring me proof you can handle yourself.' Her voice holds steady, but her hands don't.
Ch1_P4.Title: Trial by Scrap

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

3.Description: Go to Scrap Fields in Goblin Junkyard

5.Description: Bring the Scrap Metal to Marta

4.Description: Kill Cog Crabs and collect Scrap Metal (0/3)

Ch2_P1.NarrativeText: The wreckage is cleared. The ground where the house stood looks so much bigger with everything gone... Theron said work is the best thing for today. Fine, a chicken, then.
Ch2_P1.Title: Something to Feed

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

1.speaker: Hogan
1.text: A chicken! Good choice, she's the easiest animal to start with, and she'll bawk at ya when somethin's wrong.

4.speaker: Hogan
4.text: Set her in the plot, feed her, and talk to her sometimes. They listen better than most folks.

3.speaker: Hogan
3.text: Take a hay bundle too. Keep her trough full and she'll grow nice and strong, then she'll lay for ya.

2.speaker: Hogan
2.text: This one likes ya already. See how she tips her head?

3.DialogueGreeting: Ah, hello, neighbor! Heard the hammering up the road. What can I do for ya?

2.Description: Open Build mode and place your Animal Plot

5.Description: Buy a Hay Bundle (from Hogan, or Rendall at night)

6.Description: Put your chicken in the Animal Plot

Ch2_P3.NarrativeText: Theron waves you in before you knock. The tea is already poured. He asks his questions gently and you answer all but one. The letter stays in your pocket.
Ch2_P3.Title: The Elder's Guidance

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

3.Description: Ask Neria for a skill book

1.speaker: Neria
1.text: Skill books are on the job shelves, cleric, enchanter, warrior, defender, so buy the one for YOUR job! People buy the wrong shelf every week and then cry at me like it's my fault.

3.speaker: Neria
3.text: You are lucky. I only stock true copies, clean print, no missing pages. I check every single one myself!

2.speaker: Neria
2.text: It does nothing in your bag. Open the bag and read it.

3.DialogueGreeting: If you are here to fold pages, leave. If you are here to read, come sit anywhere.

2.ChoiceLabel: You said you could help me.

1.speaker: Theron
1.text: I did, and I meant it. But first, forgive an old man's worry. Did anything of hers turn up in the wreckage? A note, a keepsake, anything at all?

3.speaker: Theron
3.text: Now, to business. The world past the fence put you down once. And it will do it again unless you're ready.

2.speaker: Theron
2.text: Hmm, nothing?... Then we let it rest, and forgive an old man for asking.

5.speaker: Theron
5.text: Then have Eren look at that weapon of yours. It needs an edge.

4.speaker: Theron
4.text: Neria sells skill books at the library. Buy the one for your job and learn it.

6.speaker: Theron
6.text: Go on, then. I will be here, I am always here.

2.DialogueGreeting: Come in, come in, the kettle's just boiled, sit yourself down.

5.Description: Learn the skill from your backpack

4.Description: Buy your job's skill book from Neria

6.Description: Place your new skill in a quick slot

1.speaker: Eren
1.text: Decent bones, bad edge. It can be better than this!

3.speaker: Eren
3.text: Ye have solite already? Good, three is aplenty for a first heat, so don't waste it.

2.speaker: Eren
2.text: Take it off first, I can't work a blade you're wearing. Then bring it to the bench with a solite stone.

8.ChoiceLabel: Theron sent me here about my weapon.
8.DialogueGreeting: Hold it up. Don't tell me what it is, let me look.

Ch4_P4.Title: The Stranger

1.text: N... not... hhhkk... mad... I was not... rrrgh...

4.text: Hhhk... h... help... please... rrrgh... help...

3.speaker: @Player
3.text: (Only last night she was standing right where I am now... if I run, I might still catch her.)

2.speaker: @Player
2.text: (Mad...? Hmm, wait. They called him mad and he went to the forest, that's what Father wrote in his letter, so this is him? The man Father came all this way to find?)

1.ChoiceLabel: What are you?!
Help you how?

1.text: My head... everything is spinning... and my hand, I can't feel my hand...

1.ChoiceLabel: Wait, don't look at it yet...

3.ChoiceLabel: You asked me to bring you to her.

2.ChoiceLabel: You came out of the swirl like that.

5.ChoiceLabel: I think my father knew you.

9.ChoiceLabel: I don't even know who she is.

12.ChoiceLabel: My mother, she came here last night.

10.ChoiceLabel: You led me to that stone.

3.DialogueGreeting: Hhh... I feel... so much better... was that you? Thank you... thank you so much.

1.Line: He's waking up... he's actually waking up.

5.Description: Ask him about the black circle

1.text: A black seal... I've seen this kind before, back at the Castle. Only the shadow assassins of Tribridge use magic this dark.

1.ChoiceLabel: Shadow assassins?

3.ChoiceLabel: Then how do we get past it?

2.ChoiceLabel: Someone sent them after my father?

5.DialogueGreeting: Stop! Don't go any closer to that circle.

4.Description: Follow him under the great tree

Ch4_P4.NarrativeText: The potion worked. The swirl pulled you in and threw you out somewhere else in the forest, and right behind you came a man with an arm of bare bone.

Ch1_P1.NarrativeText: Light, and warmth, and a ceiling you have never seen, and somewhere close, your mother. Reach for something. What you grab is the path you take.
Ch1_P1.Title: First Steps

1.Description: Open your eyes to a new world

3.Description: Find something to test your strength on

5.Description: Take down the training dummy with your upgraded skill

6.Description: Lock on and destroy the training dummy once more

Ch3_P2.NarrativeText: The stone lit up red and gave something back, a rune stone of some sort.
Ch3_P2.Title: Not From This World

1.Description: Tell Klepon what the altar did

1.speaker: Klepon
1.text: Ah... I understand now. It gave you the rune stone from the centre? So that is its purpose, then.

2.speaker: Klepon
2.text: The little one told me there are three more stones like this one, one more up above this yard, and two in the town. A man came here years ago, he brought me bread, long before the little one ever did. He made all four of them work... and left.

1.ChoiceLabel: It lit up red, and I took the rune stone in the center.
A man? When?

2.ChoiceLabel: Where is the other one in the junkyard?

1.DialogueGreeting: I heard the stone take them, one, two, three, four... Tell me, what happened when the last piece went in?

1.Line: A man, years ago, bringing bread to a blind goblin and making these stones work? Who does that?

2.Line: Someone was looking for something, someone who did not want to be found... It is probably nothing, but I cannot stop thinking about that man.

3.Description: Find the stone ball under the fallen bridge

2.Description: Find the stone on the cliff

1.Line: Just a stone base with nothing on it. Something used to sit here, and it is gone.

3.Line: Two moons... whoever drew this is not from here. Whatever sat on this stone base, I will have to find it first.

2.Line: And there are two drawings on the rock behind it... one is a city of towers with goblins dancing, under what looks like two moons? And the other is a pile of scrap under a single moon, with one goblin sitting alone.

5.Description: Set the ball and the ring on the stone base (0/2)

1.Line: The ball sits in the base and points the whole thing, while the ring turns around it like a dial...

3.Line: And once the ball is in the right position, the arrow on the ring should point toward the two moons in the drawing. Let's see...

2.Line: The goblins came up here at night to watch the moons, Klepon said. So the ball... its marks should face the direction the moon sets.

4.Description: Dig the stone ring out of the trash heaps

7.Description: Take the rune from the pedestal in the trash heaps

6.Description: Align the stone until it finds the sky with two moons

1.Line: It lit up! The arrow is pointing at the two moons, and the ball is facing the direction the moon sets.

3.Line: Nothing came out of it, so the other rune stone, the one I could take from a pedestal, must be down in the heaps, just as we figured out.

2.Line: Two moons... is that the sky they came from? This world only has one...

Ch3_P4.NarrativeText: The sky over the town turned cyan and magenta. One more stone left in the town, Klepon will want to hear about this one too.
Ch3_P4.Title: The Color With No Name

1.Description: Tell Klepon the sky turned colorful

1.speaker: Klepon
1.text: Ah, yes, blue... so that is what you call it. Ha... twice in my life, then. And still, nobody came for us. Well... there is one more stone left.

1.ChoiceLabel: Green sky? But it is blue... And it turned colorful!
Where is it?

3.ChoiceLabel: Then I will find it too.

1.DialogueGreeting: Three of them now, I can hear it... Tell me, did the town breathe once more? Did the green sky turn colourful again?

1.Line: A color they see as green, but I see as blue? He spent a whole winter at those pillars working that out.

2.Line: Whatever he was looking for, he found it there.

3.Description: Find the yellow cog in the market area

2.Description: Find the two pillars past the Crown Mound gate

1.Line: Two pillars, and two empty sockets at the foot of each. Whatever sat in them is gone.

3.Line: The man turned these pillars blue. If I want to see what he saw, I need the four cogs first.

2.Line: A color they have no word for. They stood under it every day and never once saw it as blue.

4.Description: Find the orange cog in the trash near the dump trestle

7.Description: Set the four cogs into the pillars (0/4)

1.Line: Cyan, magenta, yellow, and orange. Looks like the color of their steam and fire. Four cogs, and every one of them can turn.

3.Line: But turning one cog drags the two on the other pillar with it... I need to solve this.

2.Line: The pillars need to be blue, the color of the sky. Blue is cyan and magenta together, with no yellow and orange.

1.Line: That is the last one, go back to the pillars.

9.Description: Take the rune from the pedestal behind the Junk King's throne

8.Description: Turn the cogs until both pillars glow blue

1.Line: Blue!

2.Line: They stood here mixing every color there is, and the one they were looking for was above their heads the whole time...

Ch1_P3.NarrativeText: Tools in hand, seeds in your pack. Marta watches from the doorway as you step onto the plot. 'Soil won't break itself,' she says. 'Hoe first. Then plant, water, wait, and wait, and more waiting.'
Ch1_P3.Title: Working the Land

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

3.Description: Till soil on your farm plot (0/5)

1.speaker: Marta
1.text: Here. Wheat seeds, my own stock. Five of them, a hardy strain that'll come up in any season.

3.speaker: Marta
3.text: Five patches. If you mess up we'll start over, and I don't want to hear a word about it!

2.speaker: Marta
2.text: Soil won't break itself. Hoe first. Then plant, water, wait, and wait, and more waiting.

2.DialogueGreeting: You bought everything? Show me... Good. No snacks, and you came straight back. That's how it's done.

Ch4_P1.NarrativeText: His page said he went into the forest after the man the Castle called mad. Everyone in the village says that forest was a good place once.
Ch4_P1.Title: The Old Forest

1.Line: The fire only just went out, there are still embers in it, and there is a fish next to it that nobody cooked.

3.Line: Father wrote that he came into this forest, but that was years ago and this fire went out just now... whoever this is, they are only a little ahead of me.

2.Line: There is a bedroll under the mushroom too, so they slept here and then left without eating.

5.Line: Wait, what is that sound... is someone snoring up there?

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Mmm... yes, this is the good stuff. Alright, a deal is a deal, so here is what I saw.

3.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
3.text: Then she sat by that fire for days, watching the trees, like she was waiting for someone. And one night a man came out of the trees, and she left with him.

2.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
2.text: The woman who lit that fire wore village clothes, old and dirty, and her hair was cut short. She came in fast and kept looking behind her, like someone was chasing her.

3.Description: Bring three Memory Sap to Grandpa Dutzie

1.ChoiceLabel: Where did they go?

3.DialogueGreeting: Krokk! Is that sap I smell? Give it here, give it here!

1.Line: Short hair, village clothes, running from someone and waiting for someone... that has to be Mother.

2.Line: So she was here, and someone came to get her, and Grandpa knows where that someone lives.

2.Description: Find where the snoring comes from

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Of course I can talk. You humans never come close enough to hear me, that is all. Now what do you want? I was having a very good dream, there was a fly in it.

1.ChoiceLabel: Did you see who lit that fire?

3.ChoiceLabel: Fine, I will get your sap.

2.DialogueGreeting: Whoa! A human! Do not sneak up on a sleeping frog like that, I thought you were a monster!

1.Line: A frog that answers questions with questions and charges for the rest... fine. I get him three Memory Sap and then he talks.

Ch2_P2.NarrativeText: The chicken is fed and the house is still quiet. Somebody in the village must have seen something that night, so ask around.
Ch2_P2.Title: Asking Around

1.Description: Open your Quest Book and claim your reward

1.speaker: Breda
1.text: I held the line with my shield up, and every soul in the village that night stood behind me... Eren with his hammer, the librarian, even Rendall with his bare hands!

3.speaker: Breda
3.text: That's all I'll say about the war today.

2.speaker: Breda
2.text: It came out of a portal. I saw portals during the war. They never open for nothing. Someone, somewhere, had a reason.

5.speaker: Breda
5.text: When your blade's done, come see me and I'll give you a fair trade.

4.speaker: Breda
4.text: One more thing. I walked the field after, and your mother wasn't among the villagers. I counted.

3.ChoiceLabel: You were a soldier. What attacked us?
3.DialogueGreeting: You're standing straighter than last month, good.

1.speaker: Arlette
1.text: Saw it? I was out there with everyone else, flingin' ladles and brooms and whatever. You'd be surprised what a broom does at speed!

3.speaker: Arlette
3.text: Come by any morning, though. Growing folk like you need to eat decent food if you're gonna put some strength on those bones.

2.speaker: Arlette
2.text: But... I never saw your mother in the crowd. It was all smoke and noise, and then it was over. I'm so sorry.

5.speaker: Arlette
5.text: Take the lunch. And come back at supper if you need some company, alright?

4.speaker: Arlette
4.text: My gramps used to tell strange stories about this village. Travelers with empty eyes, portals in the old tales. I only half listened. Wish I'd asked him more.

2.ChoiceLabel: Did you see anything that night?
2.DialogueGreeting: Oh, you're up and about! Here, I packed you a lunch, and shush, no arguing, it's already wrapped up.

5.Description: Check the season marker by your minimap

4.Description: Ask Leaf what grows this season

1.speaker: Leaf
1.text: Every seed has its season. Wheat likes spring, pumpkins want autumn. Plant in the wrong season and nothing will come up.

4.speaker: Leaf
4.text: Your mother bought pumpkin seeds from me every autumn. Paid early, and she never haggled. I will keep some aside, for when you are ready to plant again.

3.speaker: Leaf
3.text: See the season mark beside your map? Tap it, it tells you the season.

2.speaker: Leaf
2.text: I only stock what grows this season. If it's on my cart today, it'll take root in your soil today. Simple as that.

4.ChoiceLabel: What can grow this time of year?
4.DialogueGreeting: Ah, little sprout. I hope the soil at your farm is alright.

Ch3_P5.NarrativeText: Four stones in the bag. Klepon says the man went to the cliff, and his footprints stopped at the wall.
Ch3_P5.Title: This Door Is Mine

1.Description: Tell Klepon the pillars turned blue

1.speaker: Klepon
1.text: Ha! Four of them... I can hear them knocking about in there. He had four in his bag as well, eating my bread and asking his thousand questions... Then off he went, and I have been saving up answers for him ever since.

1.ChoiceLabel: They did. That is four done now...
Where did he go after that?

3.ChoiceLabel: Then I will go and see.

1.DialogueGreeting: You have returned! Did the pillars turn blue, the way they did for him?

1.Line: The man put every piece back and left without a word, and Klepon still expects him to come down the river one of these days.

2.Line: Well, I am the second one with four stones, and I am going to be the one who comes back.

3.Description: Set the four rune stones on the pedestals (0/4)

1.Line: The rune on the door is lighting up... red, yellow, blue, green, one after another.

2.Line: All four are in place. Let's see how this door opens.

2.Description: Find the cliff wall where the man vanished

1.Line: This might be the wall where the little one kept losing him.

3.Line: Empty pedestals, like the ones the stones came from. Perhaps the stones go here?

2.Line: The altar lit up, the tower and the pillars too. But this one hasn't.

1.Line: Somebody lived here. A bed, sacks, and loaves gone hard.

2.Line: He wrote all over the walls too... Let's figure out what he was doing in here.

1.Line: Whoa, the whole slab is going up, and the ground is shaking!

2.Line: There is a light on inside... well, I did not come all this way to stand outside.

6.Description: Look at the book on the desk

1.Line: A book full of his writing... The last page is not notes at all. Is it a letter?

4.Line: I think I should go to the forest... I miss my mother, and I want to see my father...

3.Line: I mean it plain... she ended her letter with those exact words. This must be him...

2.Line: The eyes... Mother wrote that. So I go, and the eyes go with me.

Ch4_P2.NarrativeText: Grandpa Dutzie says the man who came for her lives in a little house deep in the woods, past the great tree, and he knows the way. He is taking you there himself.
Ch4_P2.Title: Into the Woods

1.Description: Tell Grandpa Dutzie you are ready
1.ChoiceLabel: I am ready, take me to the house.

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Good. Stay close, little human. If you fall behind I will wait, but I will not come back for you.

1.DialogueGreeting: So? Are we going, or are you going to stand there and look at my mushroom?

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Because last night, when she went off with that man, I wanted to know where they were going, so I followed them all the way here. Just as they got to the door, a dagger came out of nowhere and hit the door right next to her head.

1.ChoiceLabel: A dagger?! Were they hurt?

2.ChoiceLabel: Why did you not tell me before?

8.DialogueGreeting: This is it, that is his house. I am not going any closer.

1.Line: Somebody tried to kill Mother... and it was only last night.

2.Line: The dagger is still stuck in the door, so whoever threw it must have been hiding behind that tree.

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: That is exactly what I was hoping you would say, little human, so carry them over the stones one at a time... and keep an eye on them, because they fight like hungry fish the moment nobody is watching.

3.DialogueGreeting: Krokk... all three of my grandchildren, and not one of them can get across a little river, so do not look at me like that, my knees are older than this whole forest.

4.Description: Help the little frogs cross the river

7.Description: Follow Grandpa Dutzie to the little house

1.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
1.text: Thank you for looking after my grandchildren... now run along home, you three, and if I hear one more word about flies I will eat them all myself!

2.speaker: Grandpa Dutzie
2.text: As for us, the little house is not far from here, so stay close and follow me, and try to keep up this time.

6.DialogueGreeting: Krokk... all three on this side and nobody got bitten, so maybe you are not as hopeless as you look, little human.

Ch4_P5.Title: The Third Stone

1.Line: A big stone arch covered in strange marks, with two small stones in the dirt in front of it, and a third one broken off at its base.

2.Line: It looks like a gate... but there's nothing behind it, just rock. Is this where Mother and Father went?

1.text: It's a portal... a real one. See those three patches in front of it? Each one holds a rune stone, and the stones feed it. But look at the third one... somebody broke it right off its base.

1.ChoiceLabel: Somebody broke it?

2.DialogueGreeting: So this is where the magic was coming from...

1.text: I know... maybe it's because I came out of a portal myself. Whatever it is, I haven't felt this strong in my whole life.

1.ChoiceLabel: So can we go through it?

4.DialogueGreeting: It works...! Can you feel that? So much mana... my whole body is answering it.

1.text: Ha... I never did tell you, did I. They call me the Mad Sage. I spent my whole life studying magic, so much that people said I'd lost my mind.

2.speaker: Mad Sage
2.text: The Council threw me out of the Castle. They said my research was too dangerous... maybe they were right, maybe they were wrong.

6.ChoiceLabel: Whoa, what is this?! Who are you?!

1.ChoiceLabel: So what can you do for me?

Ch4_P5.NarrativeText: The black seal is gone, and the stranger ran straight into the cave behind it. At the very end he stopped in front of a big stone arch.

SilentWatcher.NarrativeText: Theron's always close when the monsters come. Never lifts a hand. Asks about your finds a little too eager. And the stronger you get, the more of them show up.. Once you caught him talking to no one behind the Elder House. Watch the watcher.
SilentWatcher.Title: Silent Watcher

TheSaddestSmile.NarrativeText: Arlette stops wiping the counter. 'Grandfather used to tell me about a man who wandered in here once. Didn't know his own name. Had this smile like he'd lost something he couldn't even remember having.' She looks up at you. 'You asking after your father.. reminded me.'
TheSaddestSmile.Title: The Saddest Smile

FourHundredWinters.NarrativeText: Leaf works the soil, slow. 'There was a child once. Small hands, and magic like I'd not seen in four hundred years. Then gone. The Sages said, taken for training.' She pauses. 'They smiled when they said it. Sages don't smile when they take a child.'
FourHundredWinters.Title: Four Hundred Winters

SpecialDelivery.NarrativeText: Arlette shoves three parcels at you. 'Fertilizer for Leaf, feed for Hogan, iron ingots for Eren. I can't leave the shop, so.. before lunch, please?' She grabs your sleeve. 'If they're late, Leaf lectures me. Three hours. I won't survive another.'
SpecialDelivery.Title: Special Delivery

FishForHogan.NarrativeText: Hogan waves you over. 'My pigs are mad for salmon, the good kind out the deep river. I'd fetch it myself, but..' He tips his head at them. 'They fret when I go. Boar thing.' You don't follow. The pigs just stare at you, far too hard.
FishForHogan.Title: The Rancher's Request

TheSoldiersDebt.NarrativeText: Rendall polishes a clean glass. 'I was a captain once. Held the line against a thing that walked out of a ring of stone. Then the Sages called retreat, so we retreated.' His voice flattens. 'They cut down every last one of my men on the way home. Called it an enemy defeat.' The glass cracks in his hand.
TheSoldiersDebt.Title: The Soldier's Debt

TavernCleanup.NarrativeText: Rendall tosses you a rag. 'Soldiers every night. They drink, they brawl, they leave a mess. One hour. You clean, you pour, I pay. Deal?' Simple enough. Then you're balancing five ales for drunk guards while mopping spilled stew with your feet.
TavernCleanup.Title: A Bartender's Burden

KnowledgeUnwilling.NarrativeText: Neria doesn't look up. 'Skill books, left. Portal skill? Door's behind you. I want no part of whatever this is.' But she doesn't tell you to leave. Ask it right, and she finally shuts her book. 'Fine. Sit. This'll take a while.'
KnowledgeUnwilling.Title: Knowledge, Unwilling

TheOldForest.NarrativeText: Hogan leans on the fence. 'Lived in a forest once. Beautiful place, animals everywhere.' His voice drops. 'Then some fella in a house blew himself sky high, and it all went wrong. My beasts panicked, we ran, never went back.' He shakes his head. 'They say the chairs walk now. And the teapots bite.'
TheOldForest.Title: The Old Forest

ManufacturedWars.NarrativeText: Breda watches the embers. 'Served with a supply carrier once. Everyone called him useless. Then one night he's asleep and magic's pouring off him, more than any Sage I ever met.' She goes quiet. 'Those wars never made sense. Enemies out of nowhere, orders to keep fighting. That man was your father.'
ManufacturedWars.Title: Manufactured Wars
